title: Dressing & Fastenings
strapline: Wellies on the wrong feet, a zip half-done, a hat that's really a mitten — the proud, patient work of dressing yourself.
intent: Support toddlers to do more of their own dressing — coats, shoes, hats, zips and poppers — building real independence.
Develop the fine-motor control that fastenings demand: pinching a zip pull, lining up a popper, threading an arm into a sleeve.
Grow the persistence and self-belief that come from a child struggling with a coat and, at last, doing it themselves.
Build the sequencing and body-awareness of dressing — which goes on first, which foot, which way round.
Honour the child's 'me do it!' and give the time it truly takes, so getting-ready is learning, not a rush.
implementation: Build in plenty of time for self-dressing at the natural moments — coats for outdoors, aprons for painting, shoes after sleep.
Teach small tricks that unlock independence: the coat-flip to get arms in, a tag inside so shoes go on the right feet, holding the zip base to start it.
Offer a dressing-practice area — a busy board of zips and buttons, dolls to dress, dressing-up clothes with real fastenings.
Stand back and wait through the fumbles; step in only when frustration tips over, and offer the smallest help that unsticks them.
Name and celebrate each success — 'you did your own zip all the way up!' — and let the child feel the pride.
key_questions: Which goes on first — do you remember?
How could we check your wellies are on the right feet?
You've started the zip — can you pull it all the way up?
That popper is fiddly — what helps you line it up?
You did that all by yourself — how does that feel?

impact.text: Toddlers cooperate with and take over their own dressing — pushing arms into sleeves, pulling on hats, tackling shoes.
Children work zips, poppers and buttons with growing control, fine-motor skill building fastening by fastening.
A toddler bats away help with a stubborn coat — 'me do it!' — persists, and glows when it finally goes on.
Managing their own coat, shoes and belongings, children take real steps towards independent self-care.

enhancements: A dressing busy-board — zips, buttons, buckles, laces and poppers mounted for practice.
Dolls and teddies with real fastenings to dress and undress.
A dressing-up rail of coats, boots and hats with genuine zips and poppers.
Photo sequence cards showing the order of getting ready for outdoors.
A low peg and shoe bench so children can fetch and manage their own things.

playing_exploring: Children practise dressing through play — on dolls, in dressing-up, at the busy board.
Fastenings are explored hands-on, by trial and repeated attempt.
active_learning: Toddlers stay with a tricky zip or shoe until it works, refusing to be rescued too soon.
creating_thinking: Children work out the order and the tricks — coat-flip, right feet, zip-start — and apply them next time.
